citation: Perry E. Borchers (Ohio State University) for HABS, 'North elevation - inclined: left stereopair', copy photograph of photogrammetric plate LC-HABS-GS05-T-3224-202L, John J. Glessner House, 1800 South Prairie Avenue, Chicago, 1965. HABS IL-1015 photograph 14 of 17 (call number HABS ILL,16-CHIG,17--14). Library of Congress.
author: Perry E. Borchers (HABS)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division (HABS). Master TIFF 060916pu.tif in the owner's Internet Archive item master-pnp-habshaer-il-il0100-il0118-photos (checksummed in chicago/prairie_1904_v1/research/acquired-files.json); 1800 px web copy committed at chicago/prairie_1904_v1/research/public/glessner-habs-photo-14.jpg (Prairie library, PR #169); the index to photographs (glessner-habs-photo-captions.pdf, same folder) gives the caption and plate number.
locator: The whole plate: the east wing's 18th Street gable from the NE corner to the round tower, tilted upward so the gable apex, its datestone chimney and the tower's cone are in frame.
rights_note: Made for HABS (U.S. Government); LOC: no known restrictions. Measurements only; nothing derived as an asset.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-09-29 (T-1730, version v2) from the committed web copy. Scaled on the east-wing second-floor pair's colonnettes (W 9.6 and 28.8 on sheet 3; 18.4 px/ft at that level), principal point taken at the top and bottom fiducials (x 905). The plate is inclined, so horizontal positions high on the wall are compressed toward x 905; readings are corrected in the direction only. The caption and plate number are the HABS index to photographs; the handle follows photograph 13's record (060915p), the plates being consecutive in the master TIFF series.
note: A 1965 photogrammetric plate of the series sheet 6 was plotted from (photographs 13-17 are the Borchers plates; the index says 1-12 were transmitted earlier). Used only for masonry and roofs, which the 1946 alteration list (HABS data p. 2) does not touch.
what_it_supplies: the position of the 18th Street gable's apex and its chimney (W ~17, the chimney ~6.2 ft wide)
the round tower's cone beside the gable, and a first estimate of its axis (W ~37 after the depth correction)
the two first-floor slits and second-floor pairs of the east wing's north face
